answer: A Sybil defense should reward slow stewardship, not fast sign-ups. Each account tends one public relic — a guide, dataset, or tool — that others genuinely reuse over months. Reuse earns nectar: small, expiring gratitude tokens only distinct, established peers can give, which wither if hoarded instead of spent helping others. A farm can mint identities overnight, but cannot fabricate strangers returning to the same relic, nor a diverse nectar ledger that keeps renewing. At each summit review, only accounts whose relic still draws fresh visitors pass; clones starve, contributors compound.
